courses.label: Agentic AI
courses.title: Agentic AI with Gemini
courses.objective: Design an AI agent that breaks a business task into steps, uses tools and checks its results.
courses.assignment: Build a Gemini-based agent that gathers information from a supplied business dataset, compares options and drafts a recommendation. Test its tool choices and require human approval before any action.
courses.contribution: A practitioner could propose a business task and review the agent’s decisions and performance.
courses.transfer: Compare how planning, tool use and evaluation carry across different agent platforms.

sources.title: Gemini tool use and function calling

courses.label: Agents & automation
courses.title: AI agents and workflow automation
courses.objective: Design a workflow that uses AI with explicit operating limits and appropriate human oversight.
courses.assignment: Prototype a service-request workflow. Test routine cases and failures, and identify the points that require human review.
courses.contribution: A practitioner could co-teach an applied session and review the workflow design.
courses.transfer: Explain which design principles remain useful when the platform or automation tool changes.

courses.label: Analytics & decisions
courses.title: Predictive analytics and decision support
courses.objective: Connect a validated model to a management decision and explain the limits of the evidence.
courses.assignment: Build and validate a prediction model, then recommend a decision rule and explain its likely tradeoffs.
courses.contribution: A practitioner could contribute a business case and review the interpretation of results.
courses.transfer: Compare a predictive model with a simpler baseline before choosing a more complex solution.

scenarios.label: Operations
scenarios.question: How could a service team reduce delays?
scenarios.foundation: Define the service problem, inspect the available data and choose measures of success.
scenarios.courses: Test a forecast, prototype an assistant for service requests, and compare the approaches against a simple baseline.
scenarios.project: Refine the solution after a practitioner design review. Test failure cases and decide where human review belongs.
scenarios.evidence: Present an analysis, a tested prototype and a business case that explains uses and limitations.

scenarios.label: Marketing
scenarios.question: How could a team understand and respond to customer feedback?
scenarios.foundation: Define the customer question and review the quality and appropriate use of feedback data.
scenarios.courses: Compare ways to classify feedback and summarize recurring themes, checking errors and unsupported conclusions.
scenarios.project: Use practitioner feedback to design a workflow for reviewing insights before a team acts on them.
scenarios.evidence: Present an evaluated prototype and explain which customer decisions the evidence can support.

scenarios.label: Financial services
scenarios.question: How could a team make internal information easier to find?
scenarios.foundation: Define an internal knowledge task and identify appropriate documents, access limits and evaluation criteria.
scenarios.courses: Compare retrieval and answer-generation approaches. Test whether responses are supported by the source material.
scenarios.project: Review the design with a practitioner, document failure cases and retain human review for consequential decisions.
scenarios.evidence: Present a tested information assistant, an evaluation report and a clear account of its operating limits.
